‘Hello Minka! Great to meet you!’ Minka seems nonplussed at what I thought was an uncontroversial opening remark. There’s an awkward pause. She then helloes me back. But that’s all I get.

I had to traipse around somewhat, helloing people and being helloed, before I spotted my mother and my father, sharing shade and a spread blanket with Pete and Marie Reese and Toussaint Rennie near the back of the park.

glosses: A greeting (salutation) said when meeting someone or acknowledging someone’s arrival or presence.

examples.text: Hello, everyone.

glosses: A greeting used when answering the telephone.

examples.text: Hello? How may I help you?

glosses: A call for response if it is not clear if anyone is present or listening, or if a telephone conversation may have been disconnected.

examples.text: Hello? Is anyone there?

I made a speaking trumpet of my hands and commenced to whoop “Ahoy!” and “Hello!” at the top of my lungs. […] The Colonel woke up, and, after asking what in brimstone was the matter, opened his mouth and roared “Hi!” and “Hello!” like the bull of Bashan.

glosses: Used sarcastically to imply that the person addressed has done something the speaker considers to be foolish, or missed something that should have been obvious.

examples.text: You just tried to start your car with your cell phone. Hello?

glosses: An expression of puzzlement or discovery.

examples.text: Hello! What’s going on here?

glosses: \"Hello!\" or an equivalent greeting.

examples.text: In many new buildings, though, neighbors are venturing beyond tight-lipped hellos at the mailbox.
